# im_oauth REST-API Resource Generation Skill

## Purpose

A skill for newly publishing OAuth access-token authenticated REST-APIs to external client applications using the **OAuth provider feature** of intra-mart Accel Platform.
It adopts the approach of **batch-generating the 4 types of artifacts (scope definitions, resource URL mappings, client detail configurations, and JSSP resource implementation skeletons) from a single `spec.json` via `scripts/build-oauth.js`** (the same method as `jssp-im-workflow-generator`).
The coding agent writes only the spec.json; the detailed XML structure and JSSP common skeleton are automatically generated by the script.

## Generation Targets

- **Scope definition XML** - `src/main/conf/oauth-client-scopes-config/{feature-name}.xml`
- **Resource URL configuration XML** - `src/main/conf/oauth-client-resources-config/{feature-name}.xml`
- **Client detail configuration XML** - `src/main/conf/oauth-client-details-config/{feature-name}.xml`
- **Resource implementation .js** - `src/main/jssp/src/{feature-name}/oauth/{file}.js`

Note: For screens with presentation pages (`.html`), jobs, and workflow integration processing, use `jssp-page-generator` / `jssp-im-job-generator` / `jssp-im-workflow-usage` respectively.
Note: For regular REST-APIs called via browser tenant login sessions (with CSRF secure-token verification), use `jssp-page-generator` (this skill targets external systems).

## When to Use

When the user makes the following kinds of requests:

- "Create an OAuth REST-API"
- "Expose an API usable by external systems with OAuth tokens"
- "Add an im_oauth resource"
- "Add a new URL to oauth-client-resources-config"
- "Define a new OAuth scope"

## Integrated Workflow

**Execute this workflow in order from top to bottom. Skipping steps or changing the order is prohibited.**
Complete each step before moving to the next. Report to the user only after step 6 is complete.

---

### Step 1: Requirements Interview

Confirm the following with the user (ask if not given).

| Confirmation Item | Example |
|---------|-----|
| Feature name (directory / XML file name) | `sample_oauth`, `equipment_api` |
| API name / file name | `get_user`, `list_equipments` |
| Published URL (`path`) | `/oauth/sample_oauth/get_user` |
| HTTP method | `GET` / `POST` / `PUT` / `DELETE` |
| Query / body parameters | `userCd` required, up to 100 chars, etc. |
| Required scope (newly defined or existing) | `sample_oauth_user_read` (new) |
| **Authorization resource (`<authz>`)** | Always specify a `uri/action` authorization resource on each resource (skipping authorization via `welcome-all` is prohibited). `uri` is `service://{feature}/{api}`, and `action` is usually `execute`. See "How to Write `<authz>` and its Relationship to scope" in `reference/oauth-resources-config.md` for details. **Confirm with the user that authorization resource import materials (`jssp-tenant-setup-generator`) must also be generated** |
| Client information (use existing client or create new) | client_id, client_secret, redirect-uri |
| Business logic content | Retrieve from AccountInfoManager and return as JSON, etc. (only an outline is required because it will be manually filled in) |

For items where judgment is split, confirm with the user instead of deciding arbitrarily.

### Step 3: Assemble spec.json

Open `examples/sample_oauth.spec.json` with the Read tool to **confirm the structure**, then create `/tmp/{feature-name}.spec.json` reflecting the interview results.
The spec.json structure has a 1:1 correspondence with the reference XML, so you don't need to look at the reference to decide field names.

```jsonc
{
  "feature": "sample_oauth",                    // Feature name (directory / XML file name)
  "errorCodeProduct": "IWP",                    // Error code prefix E.{IWP}.{FEATURE}.{API}.NNNNN

  "scopes": [                                   // Multiple allowed. Standardly prepare 3 languages (ja/en/zh_CN)
    {
      "id": "sample_oauth_user_read",
      "defaultSubject": "Sample OAuth user-read scope",
      "localizations": {
        "ja": { "subject": "...", "text": "..." },
        "en": { "subject": "...", "text": "..." },
        "zh_CN": { "subject": "...", "text": "..." }
      }
    }
  ],

  "resources": [                                // URL mappings for published REST-APIs (multiple allowed)
    {
      "id": "sample-oauth-get-user",            // <client-resource id>
      "path": "/oauth/sample_oauth/get_user",   // Published URL
      "type": "jssp",                           // jssp or java
      "file": "get_user",                       // JSSP file name (without extension)
                                                //   → target becomes {feature}/oauth/{file} automatically
      "authz": { "uri": "service://sample_oauth/get_user", "action": "execute" },
                                                // Required. welcome-all is not allowed. Specifying uri/action
                                                //   outputs <authz uri="..." action="..." />
                                                //   (omitting it or specifying "welcome-all" makes build-oauth.js abort with an error)
      "scopes": ["sample_oauth_user_read"],

      "api": {                                  // JSSP skeleton generation parameters
        "title": "User Information Retrieval REST-API (OAuth Published Version)",
        "description": "...(content of @description comment)",
        "logPrefix": "sample_oauth/get_user",   // [...] prefix inside logger
        "allowedMethods": ["GET"],
        "parameters": [                         // For automatic validation generation
          {
            "name": "userCd",
            "required": true,
            "maxLength": 100,
            "pattern": "^[0-9A-Za-z_@.+!\\-]+$",
            "patternMessage": "The format of userCd is invalid."
          }
        ],
        "extraErrorCodes": [                    // Other than ERROR_CODE_INVALID_REQUEST / METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED / INTERNAL
          { "name": "USER_NOT_FOUND", "code": "00004" }
        ]
      }
    }
  ],

  "clients": [                                  // Client application registration (multiple allowed)
    {
      "clientId": "sample-oauth-client",
      "grantType": "authorization_code",
      "clientSecret": "change-me-in-production",  // Do not directly write the production value into the repository
      "redirectUri": "https://example.com/sample_oauth/callback",
      "accessTokenValiditySeconds": 3600,
      "codeChallenge": "S256",
      "defaultName": "Sample OAuth Client",
      "localizations": {
        "ja":    { "clientName": "...", "description": "..." },
        "en":    { "clientName": "...", "description": "..." },
        "zh_CN": { "clientName": "...", "description": "..." }
      },
      "scopes": ["sample_oauth_user_read"]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Notes when writing spec.json:**
- `feature` must be **lowercase snake_case** only (lowercase alphanumerics and underscores)
- `scopes[].id` must be referenced **with matching names** from `resources[].scopes[]` and `clients[].scopes[]` (mismatches are detected and errored by the build script)
- Make sure `path` does not duplicate a URL in `routing-jssp-config`. Check `src/main/conf/routing-jssp-config/` with Glob beforehand.
- Standardly **write all 3 languages** (`ja` / `en` / `zh_CN`) for `<localizations>`
- The build script automatically expands `api.parameters` into `validateRequest()`. If you express required / maxLength / regex in the spec, the corresponding validation code is generated.
- In `api.extraErrorCodes`, list only error codes other than `INVALID_REQUEST` / `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` / `INTERNAL` that are needed.

---

### Step 4: Run build-oauth.js

```bash
node {{AGENT_ROOT}}/skills/jssp-im-oauth-generator/scripts/build-oauth.js \
     /tmp/{feature-name}.spec.json
```

What build-oauth.js does automatically:
- Validates spec.json (stops immediately if scope ID mismatch, required field missing, or schema invalid)
- Generates `src/main/conf/oauth-client-scopes-config/{feature}.xml` (overwrites existing)
- Generates `src/main/conf/oauth-client-resources-config/{feature}.xml` (overwrites existing)
- Generates `src/main/conf/oauth-client-details-config/{feature}.xml` (overwrites existing)
- Generates `src/main/jssp/src/{feature}/oauth/{file}.js` (**skips with warning if file already exists**, to prevent accidental loss of business logic)
- 3-locale expansion, sequential numbering of error code constants, automatic expansion of validation function, JSDoc formatting

**Flags:**
- `--xml-only` ... Updates only the 3 XML files and does not touch JSSP. Use this to **regenerate only the XML while preserving the .js with implemented business logic when the spec is changed later**

```bash
# Spec updated → regenerate only XML (preserves JSSP business logic)
node {{AGENT_ROOT}}/skills/jssp-im-oauth-generator/scripts/build-oauth.js \
     /tmp/{feature-name}.spec.json --xml-only
```

**To forcibly regenerate the JSSP skeleton:** Manually delete the target `.js` file and rerun.

---

### Step 5: Filling in JSSP Business Logic

The JSSP skeleton generated by build-oauth.js contains:
- `init(request)` overall structure
- `checkMethod()` / `validateRequest()` (auto-expanded from `parameters` in spec)
- `throwApiError()` / `throwValidationError()`
- `sendJsonResponse()`
- `processBusinessLogic(request)` is placed as **an empty function with a TODO comment**

Manually fill in the contents of `processBusinessLogic`. Refer to the implementation examples in `reference/oauth-resource-implementation.md` and `assets/sample-oauth-get-user.md`.

**Conventions when filling in:**
- When DB access is involved, follow `{{AGENT_ROOT}}/instructions/jssp-2way-sql.instructions.md`, externalize SQL files under `src/main/jssp/src/{feature-name}/sql/`, and use `executeByTemplate`
- Do not include **confidential information (passwords, authentication tokens, unmasked personal information)** in the response JSON
- For non-existent users, etc., throw with `throwApiError(ERROR_CODE_*, 404, '...')` (constants already defined via `extraErrorCodes` in spec)

---

### Step 6: Manual Check

Since build-oauth.js auto-verifies the following, this step only checks **manual-completion items** that the script cannot detect.

> **Auto-checked by build-oauth.js:** spec.json schema, required fields, scope ID reference integrity (whether scopes referenced from resources / clients exist in `scopes[]`)

| Check Item | Confirmation |
|------------|---------|
| No URL duplication | Whether `path` in `oauth-client-resources-config` duplicates a URL in `routing-jssp-config` (check with Glob and Grep) |
| No secure token check | Whether `verifySecureToken` / `X-Intramart-Secure-Token` strings are mixed into the filled-in business logic (check with Grep) |
| **Authorization resource integrity** | Whether `<authz uri/action>` is explicitly set on each `<client-resource>` and the corresponding authorization resource import materials (generated by `jssp-tenant-setup-generator`) are prepared |
| Business logic implementation | Whether the `// TODO:` comment in `processBusinessLogic` is removed |
| jssp-page-generator script | If `validate-jssp-code.js` is available, run it against the generated `.js` |

**After completion, report to the user.**
Include the following in the report:

- The spec.json path used
- List of generated files (paths)
- Published endpoint URL (with context path assumed)
- Required scopes
- Sample request examples (`curl`, etc.)
- Whether an existing client was used / a new client was created
- The specified authorization resource (`uri/action`). **Clearly state that the next step is to generate the corresponding authorization materials with `jssp-tenant-setup-generator`**
- **Items the user should verify after deployment** (whether scope / client / resource were registered in the admin screen, whether the build filter replaced the client-secret, whether CORS allowance settings are required when accessed from a different origin, etc.)

---

## Common Failure Patterns

- **Writing secure token verification**: Unnecessary in OAuth REST-APIs. Writing it by mistake causes clients that only hold OAuth access tokens to be rejected with 400
- **Creating `.html` pair files**: OAuth resources do not return HTML, so pair files do not need to be created
- **Mismatching scope IDs between resources-config and details-config**: Inconsistencies occur such as the client unable to request the scope or the resource requiring an unavailable scope
- **Duplicating `path` with routing-jssp-config**: Causes conflicts in the platform-side dispatching
- **Writing the production client-secret directly in the repository**: Leak risk. Use filter substitution or per-environment configuration replacement
